title: Write Feature tests for the shipping quote API
summary: Hit the quote API with RefreshDatabase and actingAs, swap the carrier API for Http::fake, trip over post() turning a 422 into a 302, and stop stray requests with preventStrayRequests.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Http\Resources\QuoteResource;
use App\Services\CarrierClient;
use Illuminate\Http\Client\ConnectionException;
use Illuminate\Http\Client\RequestException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class QuoteController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request, CarrierClient $carrier)
    {
        $validated = $request->validate([
            'postal_code' => ['required', 'digits:7'],
            'weight_grams' => ['required', 'integer', 'min:1', 'max:30000'],
        ]);

        try {
            $fee = $carrier->rate($validated['postal_code'], $validated['weight_grams']);
        } catch (ConnectionException|RequestException $e) {
            report($e);

            return response()->json(['message' => 'Carrier unavailable'], 502);
        }

        $quote = $request->user()->quotes()->create([...$validated, 'fee' => $fee]);

        return new QuoteResource($quote);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Services;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

class CarrierClient
{
    public function rate(string $postalCode, int $weightGrams): int
    {
        return Http::withToken(config('services.carrier.token'))
            ->timeout(5)
            ->post('https://api.carrier.example/v2/rates', [
                'to' => $postalCode,
                'weight' => $weightGrams,
            ])
            ->throw()
            ->json('amount');
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Resources;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Resources\Json\JsonResource;

class QuoteResource extends JsonResource
{
    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        return [
            'id' => $this->id,
            'postal_code' => $this->postal_code,
            'weight_grams' => $this->weight_grams,
            'fee' => $this->fee,
        ];
    }
}

turns.user: QuoteController has zero tests. write some. do NOT hit the real carrier api, we get billed per call. phpunit, not pest

assistant.body: Great call! Here are two tests in tests/Feature/QuoteTest.php. RefreshDatabase rebuilds the database for each test, and actingAs sends the request as a logged in user. CarrierClient goes through the Http facade, so Http::fake on api.carrier.example keeps every call away from the real API.

Note: assertJsonPath and assertJson check different things. assertJsonPath compares one path with ===, so 980 and '980' are not the same. assertJson is a subset match, so values that change every run, like id, can be left out. Http::assertSent at the end checks that the postal code and the token were really sent.

<?php

namespace Tests\Feature;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Illuminate\Http\Client\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;
use Tests\TestCase;

class QuoteTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    public function test_it_stores_the_fee_from_the_carrier(): void
    {
        config(['services.carrier.token' => 'test-token']);
        Http::fake([
            'api.carrier.example/*' => Http::response(['amount' => 980]),
        ]);
        $user = User::factory()->create();

        $this->actingAs($user)
            ->post('/api/quotes', ['postal_code' => '1500001', 'weight_grams' => 1200])
            ->assertCreated()
            ->assertJsonPath('data.fee', 980)
            ->assertJson(['data' => ['postal_code' => '1500001']]);

        $this->assertDatabaseHas('quotes', ['user_id' => $user->id, 'fee' => 980]);
        Http::assertSent(fn (Request $request) => $request['to'] === '1500001'
            && $request->hasHeader('Authorization', 'Bearer test-token'));
    }

    public function test_it_rejects_a_zero_weight(): void
    {
        Http::fake();

        $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create())
            ->post('/api/quotes', ['postal_code' => '1500001', 'weight_grams' => 0])
            ->assertUnprocessable()
            ->assertJsonValidationErrors('weight_grams');

        Http::assertNothingSent();
    }
}

turns.user: second one fails. Expected response status code [422] but received 302.

assistant.body: Apologies, using post() was my mistake. post() sends no Accept: application/json header, so Laravel treats the failed validation as a form submission and redirects back. postJson() gets the JSON 422 instead. The first test passed only because the Resource answers with JSON on success.

turns.user: green. now one for when the carrier is down, 503 should give us a 502. also scared a test without a fake will hit prod someday, can we block that?

assistant.body: Sure. Http::fake only swaps requests that match a pattern, and anything else goes out to the network as usual. Calling Http::preventStrayRequests() in setUp turns every unfaked request into a StrayRequestException, so the test fails instead. The 503 test also checks that no quote was saved.
